# corral

> corral audits whether a test suite actually tests anything. A model plants deliberate, goal-violating faults in your code, your project's own test command runs against each one in an offline sandbox, and the kill rate is what execution measured, never what a model reported. For each fault your tests miss, a test-writer model writes a test that catches it and corral runs it to prove so: the proven missing tests are handed back to you, and every verdict is recorded in a signed, hash-linked ledger.

corral is a Go CLI (source-available, Elastic License 2.0), solo-maintained. It audits; it never builds or edits your code. It has no default models: you name every seat (any API provider, a local model through Ollama, or a coding-agent CLI such as `claude-code` or `codex` running on its own subscription login). A second, different model critiques the suite, and its opinion is advisory: it never gates a verdict. Languages: Go, Python, Ruby, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP and Rust; what each runner supports is on the language-support page. An optional daemon (the "brain") exists, is frozen, and is not used or read by any audit.

First run: `corral certify --repo . --dry-run` lists what corral can audit (no key, no sandbox, no cost); `corral doctor` checks sandbox, toolchain and keys for free; then `corral certify --repo . --top 3 --max-tokens 3000000 --writer-model <m> --mutant-model <m> --derive-model <m> --critic-model <m> -- <your test command>`.

## Docs
- [How it works](https://corralai.dev/docs/how-it-works/): the audit, the review and the ledger, step by step
- [Getting started](https://corralai.dev/docs/getting-started/): install, a first audit, subscription agent seats, Python virtualenvs, Rust, the sandbox traps
- [Your first audit, in detail](https://corralai.dev/docs/first-audit/): one certify --local run end to end
- [The GitHub Action](https://corralai.dev/docs/github-action/): an audit on every pull request, with a merge gate
- [On an internal forge](https://corralai.dev/docs/internal-forge/): the same recipe on GitLab, Gitea and others
- [Verify a record yourself](https://corralai.dev/docs/verify-a-record/): check a published verdict offline
- [Mutants, survivors, kill rates](https://corralai.dev/docs/concepts/mutation-testing/): the vocabulary, and how this differs from classical mutation testing
- [Multi-model herds](https://corralai.dev/docs/concepts/multi-model-herds/): what decorrelation is enforced, seats on a subscription, comparing models
- [Trust & security](https://corralai.dev/docs/concepts/trust-and-security/): the offline jail, the one mode that touches your checkout, keys and seats, the signed ledger
- [The record](https://corralai.dev/docs/warehouse/): the ledger branch, DuckDB, Rekor and MotherDuck
- [Configuration](https://corralai.dev/docs/configuration/): seats, keys, agent seats, the sandbox, signing and the cache
- [Language support](https://corralai.dev/docs/language-support/): every language and runner, generated from the code's own table
- [CLI reference](https://corralai.dev/docs/cli/corral/): every binary's flags, generated from its own -h output
- [Limitations & roadmap](https://corralai.dev/docs/limitations/): what it does today, its current limits, and what it does not claim

## Field notes
- [The first Rust audit](https://corralai.dev/field-notes/the-first-rust-audit/): one file of Warp's fuzzy matcher, the faults its tests missed, and the tests corral proved
- [The auditor never builds](https://corralai.dev/field-notes/the-auditor-never-builds/): why corral audits and does not write the code it judges
- [A ledger, not a log](https://corralai.dev/field-notes/a-ledger-not-a-log/): verdicts as signed, hash-linked files on a git branch

## More
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/pdbethke/corralai): the code, Elastic License 2.0
- [Recordings](https://corralai.dev/recordings/): replayable tapes of real audits
- [The public record](https://corralai.dev/ledger/): corral's own ledger, entry by entry
